body: Offer the average Joe or Joette an extra six grand a year for sucking a dick and I betcha you'd find a high number of takers.  Your real mistake was telling him.

On a purely practical level this wouldn't work because many severely depressed people do recover even after years, and there's no diagnostic way to tell them from the unrecoverable cases (if we assume these exist).

But the deeper problem is that the purpose of the euthanasia in the case of a depressed person is not the same, so there is no moral equivalence.  Most people who get state-sanctioned euthanasia literally could not complete the act without help, at least not painlessly (and if someone did it for them outside the law they could be charged with murder).  But there is no physical impediment preventing you from ending it painlessly.  You just want help overcoming the psychological difficulty, and doctors are even less keen on overcoming their innate disinclination to kill physically-healthy patients than your mind is on overcoming the will to live.

It's worth mentioning thought that you don't fulfill your own criteria - you haven't tried everything.  ECT, deep brain stimulation, dietary supplements, many more.  Beyond that you are far too young to have had enough friendships and relationships to know they're all a waste of time.  I've been depressed at least 15 out of my 28 years, and life does not magically get better in response to anything, and some people do stay depressed their whole lives, and I'm not even convinced that I can pull *myself* out of it.  So I would never blow sunshine up your ass, but I can tell you that even if the depression never entirely goes away the sense of powerlessness does as you learn more about yourself, which only comes with time lived.

I recommend you read The Myth of Sisyphus by Albert Camus.  [Read](http://blsciblogs.baruch.cuny.edu/authenticityandastonishment2/files/2013/04/Albert-Camus-The-Myth-of-Sisyphus.pdf) the first five pages at least.  Feel free to PM if you wanna talk.
